titulo: From your first agent to a small team in 30 days
lead: The most common mistake is setting up five agents on the first weekend and stopping the review by Tuesday. The approach that works starts slowly: one task, review everything, build trust, and only then add the next. In four weeks, you'll have a small team working while you review a sample of its work.
objetivo: build a four-week plan with full review at the beginning, sampling later, and one new task each week.

aprende.t: The four weeks, one at a time
When to review everything and when to sample
The log that proves it worked
Your plan with dates for the calendar

degraus.saida: First agent with a sheet and rules.
degraus.passo: Find the task (lesson 1), write the sheet (lesson 2), and run it. Check every result this week, no exceptions.

degraus.saida: Task 1 as a routine and contacts with a gate.
degraus.passo: Keep checking all of Task 1 (for a weekly task, the first three rounds are three weeks). Add a calendar reminder and Task 2: contacts (lesson 4), which runs several times a week.
Paste the routing rule into the Projects and do task 3: invoices and bills (lesson 5). Task 1 completes the three rounds and moves on to the sample.
Task 4: new client checklist (lesson 6). Once a week, read the check log, adjust one sheet, and decide which task to add next.

resultado.texto: Four boring tasks off your hands, each with a sheet, gate, and check log.

secoes.legenda: An error? That task goes back to being checked in full until three consecutive runs match.

secoes.sub: The proof it worked is the log, not your impression. Click each phase.

texto: For each agent’s first three rounds, check the entire result: every number, every draft. For a weekly task, that means three weeks; for a daily task, three days.
Every correction you make becomes a rule on the sheet.
Three rounds in a row without corrections? Move on to the sample: two numbers from the report, one draft out of every three, two invoices from the table.
The gate never goes away: you keep reading anything that talks to a client or handles money.
Found an error in the sample? That task goes back to "check everything" until three consecutive runs match again.
The error becomes a rule on the sheet before the next run.
One line per run: date, agent, what you checked, whether it matched, and what changed on the sheet.
In a month, the log shows how much time you saved and where the agent makes mistakes.

blocos.rot: Friday review (paste into the chat with the check log)
blocos.conteudo:
Here’s my check log for the week.
Tell me, in no more than 8 lines:
1. How many minutes the agents saved in total (add up the last column).
2. Which agent needed the most corrections and what rule I should add to their sheet.
3. Which agent is ready to move to spot checks (three rounds in a row with no corrections).
Don’t make up numbers: use only what’s in the log.

abas.html: In chat, you’re in charge of the schedule: the plan below creates an .ics file with reminders for your calendar ("Monday 9 a.m.: report"). Getting the agent to run on its own at the scheduled time takes a terminal step, which the course From chat to agent shows you. Start with the reminder: calling the agent at the right time already takes the boring work off your hands.

• Five agents in the first week: you can’t check everything, and the first mistake slips through.
  • Stop checking because "it’s always worked": spot checks mean checking less, not stopping.
  • No log: after a month, you won’t know whether the agent saves time or just shifts the work around.

secoes.sub: Four questions about the whole course.

perguntas.p: When can an agent move from "check everything" to "spot checks"?
opcoes: After three rounds in a row with no corrections.
Right in the first week, if the text is well written.
perguntas.explica: Three rounds in a row with no corrections show that the sheet is solid. Well written text doesn’t prove the numbers are right, and checking everything forever takes away the benefit of the agent.

perguntas.p: You found a wrong number during a spot check. What now?
opcoes: Ignore it: it was just one.
Switch all agents to the top model.
Fix the number by hand right away and keep checking only a sample, as before.
Check that task in full again, and add the error as a rule to the sheet.
perguntas.explica: An error in the sample means there’s a gap in the sheet. Go back to checking everything until you get three clean rounds in a row, then add a new rule to close the gap.

perguntas.p: Which rules apply to every agent in the course?
opcoes: Read-only, drafts only, you handle the login, and you approve all spending.
Always use the top model, always with database access.
Send simple things on its own and ask before doing anything else.
Password in AGENTS.md and automatic sending every Monday.
perguntas.explica: The four rules on the sheet protect you in every task: the agent reads and prepares; you log in, approve, send, and pay.

perguntas.p: What is the “minutes saved” column in the log for?
opcoes: To charge the agent for the time spent.
So the model knows when to stop working and how many minutes it still has left this week.
To show, at the end of the month, how much time the agents actually gave back to you.
perguntas.explica: Without a number, your impression can be misleading. The total minutes saved shows whether it’s worth assigning the next task or adjusting the ones you already have.

itens.texto: One boring task, one sheet, check everything. Start the next only when you trust it.
Read-only, drafts only, you handle the login, and you approve all spending. Use a light model for routine work and a top model for difficult tasks.
Check everything, then check samples and keep notes. In 30 days, you’ll know how much time you’ve saved.
